2018_117_011618org_regmtg.paragraph: Agenda packet for the Troy Board of Education's organizational and regular meeting of January 16, 2018 at the Services Building. The organizational half elects officers, appoints the treasurer, and settles depositories, legal counsel and the meeting schedule; the regular half ratifies a three-year extension of the TESPA support-staff contract through June 30, 2022, approves an $853,231.22 furniture purchase for 4th and 5th grade classrooms, and re-adopts an $82,700.00 asbestos abatement award after the December 19, 2017 resolution named the wrong contractor.
2018_117_011618org_regmtg.page:
**Meeting**
Organizational and regular meeting, January 16, 2018, 7:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois.

**The organizational half**
The Board elects an acting chairperson to officiate until a president is elected and appoints a temporary secretary, then elects president, vice president and secretary in turn. The treasurer is appointed, fund depositories and the investment resolution established, board and district legal counsel designated, the superintendent designated deputy secretary, a person designated for posting notices of meetings, and the meeting schedule adopted. Several of these agenda-index lines carry the prior year's dates — the depositories item reads 2016/17 and 2017/18 and the schedule item reads 2017 calendar year — apparently unrevised template text in a January 2018 packet, as is the consent-agenda line reading "Treasurer's Report – November 2016."

**Recognition**
The Mission Moment recognizes the 2017-18 Superintendent Student Advisory Board, made up of student leaders from all four high schools who are nominated by teachers, counselors and administrators and whose expressed mission is "leaving the Troy School District better than it was when they entered." The day before the meeting they carried out another Martin Luther King, Junior, Day of Service at Athens High School, where community members learned about Dr. King's legacy and performed four service projects; the SSAB also runs a smaller spring service project and advises Dr. Machesky and central office staff from a high school perspective. The second item is Board of Education Recognition, marking January as the month the district celebrates the Board's work, framed around the journey begun a little over three years earlier to become a World Class School District by 2020.

**Consent agenda**
Minutes of the December 5, 2017 special meeting and workshop and the December 19, 2017 meeting, the Treasurer's Report, and a corrected resolution from the December 19 asbestos abatement award.

**Treasurer's Report**
General Fund check disbursements total $6,816,514.12 and total disbursements in period are $9,875,817.28.

**The corrected asbestos resolution**
The packet carries both versions of the same award, which is why it is back before the Board. An RFP sought competitive bids for asbestos abatement at Costello, Martell, Morse and Leonard elementary schools; Rob Carson reviewed them. The corrected resolution awards the work to **Qualified Abatement at $82,700.00** from the 2016 Capital Projects Fund. The superseded December 19 version is reproduced with the contractor name struck through — "NOVA Environmental, Inc.Qualified Abatement" — and the amount rendered "$82,700.00.00", an evident transcription error in the original that the correction resolves.

**Personnel and business**
The Board ratifies an extension of the Troy Educational Support Personnel Association (TESPA), MEA/NEA contract **through June 30, 2022** — three years added to the existing collective bargaining agreement — and issues a probationary contract to Rebecca Turner as a 1.0 speech pathologist at Athens and the Troy Center for Transition.

The business item approves $853,231.22 of furniture for 4th and 5th grade classrooms through Workspace Interiors by Office Depot and the Oakland County America Saves Cooperative Purchase Program, as an expenditure of the 2016 Capital Projects Fund. Jennifer Gottlieb, Director of Student Growth, Equity and Accountability, led the project team with Workspace Interiors and building administrators and staff to evaluate the use and needs for furniture in those classrooms, and an accompanying "The Learning Environment" presentation sets out the design.
2018_117_011618org_regmtg.verbose:
Agenda packet for the organizational and regular meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education, January 16, 2018, 7:00 PM at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. The agenda is: 1. Pledge of Allegiance; 2. Election of Acting Chairperson; 3. Appointment of Temporary Secretary; 4. Annual Organizational Meeting of the Board of Education — A. Nomination and Election of Officers (President, Vice President, Secretary), B. Appointment of Treasurer, C. Establish Fund Depositories and Investment Resolution, D. Designation of Board and District Legal Counsel, E. Designation of Superintendent to be Deputy Secretary, F. Designation of a Person for Posting Notices of Meetings, G. Meeting Schedule; 5. Recognition — A. TSD Mission Moment: Superintendent Student Advisory Board, MLK, Jr. Day of Service, B. Board Recognition Month; 6. Additions & Deletions; 7. Public Communication (agenda items); 8. General – Consent Agenda; 9. Personnel; 10. Curriculum; 11. Business; and the remaining public communication, other and adjournment items. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. when school is in session, and viewable at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

Several agenda-index entries carry stale dates from the previous year's template: the fund depositories item is indexed as covering 2016/17 and 2017/18, the meeting schedule item reads "Meeting Schedule for 2017 Calendar Year," and the consent agenda lists "Treasurer's Report – November 2016" — all in a packet for a January 2018 meeting whose other consent items are December 2017 minutes. These are recorded here as printed rather than corrected.

**Recognition 5.A: Superintendent Student Advisory Board and the MLK Day of Service.** The Mission Moment recognizes the 2017-18 Superintendent Student Advisory Board, described as outstanding student leaders from all four high schools in the district who come together with the expressed mission of leaving the Troy School District better than it was when they entered. Members are nominated by teachers, counselors and administrators and selected from a group of applicants. The day before this meeting the students executed another successful Martin Luther King, Junior, Day of Service at Athens High School, where members of the community came together to learn about the legacy of Dr. King and perform four service projects having a direct positive impact in his name. The SSAB students helped plan and carry out the Day of Service as well as a smaller service project each spring, give input to Dr. Machesky and central office staff from a high school perspective, and work to encourage students at their own schools to participate in district-wide activities. The recommended action is to invite the students up to receive a certificate and congratulations from the Board.

**Recognition 5.B: Board of Education Recognition.** Each January the Troy School District recognizes and celebrates the work of the Board of Education. The script frames the recognition around the district's journey, begun a little over three years earlier, to become a World Class School District by the year 2020, and the Board's role in making that ambitious goal possible.

**Consent agenda.** A. Minutes of the December 5, 2017 Special Board of Education Meeting; B. Minutes of the December 5, 2017 Board of Education Workshop; C. Minutes of the December 19, 2017 Board of Education Meeting; D. Treasurer's Report; and E. Corrected Resolution from the 12/19/17 asbestos abatement award.

**Treasurer's Report.** General Fund check disbursements total $6,816,514.12, and total disbursements in period — check disbursements together with ACH debits, outgoing wire transfers, P-Card purchases and prior period void disbursements — come to $9,875,817.28. The bulk of the packet's middle sections is the check register run by fund, with roughly 1,900 register lines across parts two and three.

**Consent item 8.E: the corrected asbestos abatement resolution.** This item exists because the resolution adopted on December 19, 2017 named the wrong contractor, and the packet reproduces both versions so the Board can see the correction. Both recite the same underlying facts: an RFP was issued to obtain competitive bids for asbestos abatement work at Costello, Martell, Morse and Leonard Elementary Schools, and the bids were reviewed by Mr. Rob Carson, Director of Operations.

The corrected resolution reads that the bid for asbestos abatement at Costello, Martell, Morse and Leonard Elementary Schools be awarded to Qualified Abatement in the amount of $82,700.00, and that this amount be approved as an expenditure of the 2016 Capital Projects Fund. The superseded version is reproduced showing the edit in place — the contractor line reads "NOVA Environmental, Inc.Qualified Abatement," the original name struck through and the correct one substituted — and its amount is rendered "$82,700.00.00," a transcription error carried in the original document. The dollar figure of the award itself is unchanged at $82,700.00; what changed is the name of the firm receiving it.

**Personnel 9.A: TESPA contract extension.** The Board is recommended to approve the extension of the Troy Educational Support Personnel Association (TESPA), MEA/NEA contract through June 30, 2022 — an extension of three years to the current TESPA Collective Bargaining Agreement. The resolution approves that extension.

**Personnel 9.B: elementary and secondary.** The Board is recommended to approve the issuance of a probationary contract for the 2017-2018 school year to Rebecca Turner, 1.0 Speech Pathologist serving Athens High School and the Troy Center for Transition.

**Business 11.A: furniture purchase for 4th and 5th grade classrooms.** Jennifer Gottlieb, Director of Student Growth, Equity and Accountability, led a project team with Workspace Interiors by Office Depot and building administrators and staff to evaluate the use and needs for furniture in 4th and 5th grade classrooms. The recommendation is to approve the furniture and equipment purchase from the Oakland County America Saves Cooperative Purchase Program, and the resolution approves the furniture purchase for 4th and 5th grade classrooms in the amount of $853,231.22 through Workspace Interiors by Office Depot and the Oakland County America Saves Cooperative Purchase Program as an expenditure of the 2016 Capital Projects Fund. An accompanying presentation titled "The Learning Environment" sets out the intended classroom design and the products selected.

Read together, the January 2018 packet pairs a long-horizon labor commitment — three additional years of the TESPA agreement, running to June 30, 2022 — with the district's continuing capital reinvestment of 2016 Capital Projects Fund money into classrooms, $853,231.22 of it in this single furniture award, alongside the smaller $82,700.00 abatement contract whose only defect was the contractor's name.
